A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LASER-VFL work. Their text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; retained appendix content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on HAPT, Credit, MIMIC-IV, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, including Table 1 results across training and inference missingness conditions.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds baseline evaluations, client-count/runtime experiments, and nonuniform-missingness experiments in Figure 2 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The shared representation and fusion models, averaging aggregation, weighted objective, task-sampling procedure, and training/inference algorithms remain equivalent. Revised notation and the aggregation explanation in Appendix A.2 do not establish a changed architecture or procedure.

E1.justification: All five datasets and prediction tasks are retained. Appendix E adds a CIFAR-10 scenario with heterogeneous, Beta-distributed missingness probabilities across feature blocks, including independently sampled training and inference probabilities. This is a limited extension of input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Combinatorial and an adapted PlugVFL across all five datasets, substantially strengthening the comparator set. Combinatorial was previously only a conceptual alternative, while the work underlying PlugVFL was cited but not evaluated. Existing baselines retain their dataset participation.

E3.justification: The primary four-client missingness grid and metrics remain unchanged. Added protocols measure accuracy and runtime across two to eight clients at missingness probability 0.1, and compare Beta(2,2) block probabilities against a fixed 0.5 control. Combinatorial is omitted at eight clients because of resource constraints.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's missingness grid, v2 adds dedicated scalability and runtime analysis in Figure 2 and nonuniform-missingness robustness tests in Appendix E. These provide substantial new examinations of the method's efficiency and sensitivity to heterogeneous feature availability.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 1 means and standard deviations over five seeds. The new Table 3 follows the same practice. No changed run count, confidence-interval procedure, or significance-testing method is stated.

E6.justification: All retained Table 1 scores are unchanged, but new comparator results alter rankings: with complete HAPT training data and inference missingness 0.5, PlugVFL scores 90.3 ± 1.3 versus LASER-VFL's retained 87.0 ± 1.2. Figure 2, Appendix D runtimes, and Table 3 add substantial scaling, cost, and nonuniform-missingness findings.

T1.justification: Section 4 and the proofs replace the single variance bound sigma^2/B with separate mini-batch and task-sampling bounds, producing sigma_b^2 + K sigma_s^2 terms in both theorems. Large-batch O(1/T) and full-batch exact-convergence statements disappear. V2 also explicitly assumes missingness completely at random and adds an aggregation-equivalence derivation in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement substantially narrow the convergence claims: the large-batch O(1/T) guarantee is removed, and PL convergence is explicitly to a neighborhood of the optimum. The method's central flexibility claim remains. Abstract CIFAR-100 advantages change from 21.4%/12.2% to 18.2%/7.4%, reflecting stronger comparators rather than changed LASER-VFL scores.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking Combinatorial's behavior to training-data scarcity for larger feature subsets, discusses task-sampling variance growing with client count, and explicitly states the MCAR boundary. Appendix A.2 argues that adjusted representation models preserve aggregation expressivity. These substantially expand interpretation beyond the retained dropout-like regularization explanation.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-availability link. Appendix D newly identifies the MLP, LSTM, and ResNet18 model choices, explains PlugVFL's zero-filled missing representations and per-party dropout adaptation, and reports runtimes. These improve documentation, although detailed training hyperparameters and hardware remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ganguli et al. and supporting references for missingness mechanisms and model architectures, fixes the unresolved FedSVD citation, and expands closest-work comparisons in Appendix A.1. The central research positioning remains. Sun's updated PlugVFL reference corresponds to work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the objective and task-sampling exposition, revise notation and terminology, and expand and reorganize the appendices. The main section sequence and much of the introductory and concluding prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-panel scalability/runtime Figure 2, the LASER-VFL forward-pass diagram in Figure 3, and the nonuniform-missingness Table 3. Table 1 gains comparator rows and revised best-score emphasis. Figure 1 is relocated and its preview explicitly labeled MIMIC-IV.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for effectiveness and efficiency through relevant additional baselines, measured scaling, and heterogeneous-missingness tests that v1 lacked. Separate task-sampling variance accounting and narrower convergence claims improve theoretical qualification; implementation disclosures improve transparency. Some Section 5 wording overstates Combinatorial's dominance relative to Table 1, and training details remain limited, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains.
